stage: 1 + 2 (complete workstream) + G-cl fixes + DX fixes (G2-learn G2L-1..6, CL-10)
summary: Retrospective credit and continual learning. Stage 1 (model-independent): SqliteExperienceStore, OutcomeLinker, exact REINFORCE / all-actions / COCOA / RUDDER references, ReturnDecomposer, HindsightModel, simple attribution, EstimatorSelector, SMDP traces and credit ledger, atomic checkpoints. Stage 2 (on nn.model.CamLiveModel): ContinualLearner with one optimizer per group (never reward), per-group clipping, warm-up / cosine schedules, three timescales (fast belief update without gradient; frequent experiential + heads updates triggered by matured independent outcomes; slow adapter updates every adapter_every with a bounded adapter graph and a held-out guard: absolute, noise-measured tolerance, drift bound since the last promoted checkpoint, exact revert), measured loss shares with a 90 % cap, stratified replay, held-out split, learning records with hashes, deltas and a behavioural probe; LossProviders for RUDDER, COCOA and a bridge-grounding adapter loss; CreditAssigner (versioned per-decision credit, withheld until the return is final, evidence-selected default, credited returns); anchors + functional regularisation + measured forgetting; complete learner checkpoints, promotion / rollback on validation and retention, weights-only export and a fresh-model loader. Evidence at debug scale in LabWorld (docs/evidence/D/diagnostics.json) and single updates on Qwen3-4B + 50m core (docs/evidence/D/real_update.json). Integrated: agent.py constructs and calls the store, linker, learner, assigner, retention and checkpoint functions (verified by G2-learn; the earlier 'not integrated' statements were stale). Fix stage after the independent verification G-cl (docs/D/FIXES.md): append-only stored history with index checks, validated attribution amounts, estimator selection only on held-out lifetimes with paired standard errors (no estimator is promoted on LabWorld), provenance-gated promotion and COCOA support, full-trajectory credit, evidence regenerated from one committed tree. DX stage after G2-learn (docs/DX.md): fail-closed per-provider slow-step guard, learner-owned eligibility flags no longer shadow the providers' own, outcome timing enforced on append/update, overflow-safe attribution shares, the count mode search's convergence report, experiment records reaching the store and evidence-based estimator selection inside learn() (agent wiring: change request DX-1), checkpoints with experiment records and pending outcomes (CL-10).

RC-01.limitations: Fix stage (G-cl M3): attribution amounts in by_action / by_decision maps are validated (finite, >= 0); a map with a negative / non-finite / non-numeric amount is treated as ambiguous (equal shares of the named decisions with uncertainty); link weights of one outcome are refused when negative and renormalised above a total of 1, so the credit given for an outcome never exceeds it. Evidence kinds are structural (declared query, attribution keys in event data, parent action, artifact references, experiment arm, declared attribution windows); no learned linker. Called by the integrated agent's reconcile step (agent.py; G2-learn RC-01 verified). [DX, G2L-3] Valid amounts whose sum overflows (1e308 + 1e308) are shares relative to the largest amount (finite sums unchanged); with no stated outcome value an infinite sum is refused explicitly ('the outcome value is not finite'). Events and declared queries that measure the same consequence under different keys cannot be recognised as identical: the simple attribution therefore prefers declared answers over event links (combine='declared_first').

RC-02.limitations: Fix stage (G-cl m3): credit assignment now runs over the whole trajectory (every decision gets RUDDER credit; G and Gamma referenced at the first decision); training windows of the newest max_len decisions regress the measured return-to-go at the window's first decision, referenced there; positions beyond max_len are extrapolated by the decomposer at credit time. Now trained on the real model's decision latents (debug scale) with matured LabWorld returns; not on the real configuration beyond single updates, and not on live experience. By default the latents are detached (the regression trains the decomposer head only). The stored uncertainty of RUDDER credit is |G - F(whole trajectory)|, a proxy. 1/Gamma_t amplifies prediction error for late decisions when beta * elapsed time is large.

RC-03.limitations: Fix stage (G-cl m3): credit assignment now runs over the whole trajectory (every decision gets RUDDER credit; G and Gamma referenced at the first decision); training windows of the newest max_len decisions regress the measured return-to-go at the window's first decision, referenced there; positions beyond max_len are extrapolated by the decomposer at credit time. Convention: G is referenced at the first decision of the trajectory and Gamma_t = exp(-beta * seconds since it); conservation is sum_t Gamma_t c_t = G (max error < 1e-9 in the tests, float64 bookkeeping).

RC-04.limitations: Finite-action tabular reference only (by definition). Estimator code is adapted from the verified cam_unified implementation (provenance in the file header).

RC-05.limitations: Fix stage (G-cl m1, m2): a candidate set is open-ended when a candidate's ActionSpec.provenance names only open-ended generators (backbone, schema_sampler, mutation, ...) or the decision says so; COCOA then refuses unless proposal probabilities were tracked (default: not tracked). Unknown generator names are treated as enumerating (not open-ended). COCOA pairs now include outcomes declared by earlier decisions and observed after t (Eq. 4). Trained on the real model's beliefs and candidate embeddings at debug scale. The outcome representation is a fixed function of the outcome value (no learned outcome encoder), so outcomes of equal size are indistinguishable to the hindsight model. No sampled-alternatives estimator for candidate sets too large to enumerate. Support is judged from the logged propensities of the decision (missing / invalid / near-zero / untracked open-ended proposals); effective sample size per candidate is available in credit.cocoa but not fed by the assigner.

RC-06.limitations: When an outcome matures the linked decisions and the earlier decisions of the objective are queued, their credit is recomputed and versioned, and the learner trains on them (a share of each triggered batch is the triggering experience). Learned credit (RUDDER, COCOA) appears only when the objective is closed and nothing goal-relevant is pending; an objective that never closes never gets it. The agent has to call store.put_objective_outcome when the verifier closes an objective (change request D-10); the integrated agent does so when the verifier closes an objective (agent.py; G2-learn RC-06 verified).

RC-07.limitations: Guards at D's level: a decision after the outcome is refused as a cause; an outcome dated before its query is refused by add_outcome, and [DX, G2L-2] append() / update() raise OutcomeTimingError for a newly attached matured outcome observed before its query was issued or before its decision (stored outcomes are not re-judged; observation time 0 = unknown); add_outcome also refuses one dated before the decision when the query is unknown; stored context items cannot be rewritten; stored records cannot be rewritten either (fix G-cl M2: update() refuses changes of the decision, probabilities, context refs, provenance, results, outcomes and query definitions; every read checks the index columns against the stored content); linking never changes context_item_refs; audit_leakage() reports any context item dated after its decision. Whether the agent builds contexts correctly in the first place is outside D (audit_leakage detects it after the fact). The reference MemoryStore still overwrites items (change request D-3).

RC-08.limitations: [DX round 2] DX-1 root cause (5/28 failures of test_int2_wiring with the hook): not the hook. Replicating the test 52 times: 1/30 failures with the hook, 1/22 without (pooled with the coordinator's 6/58 vs 1/32, Fisher p 0.41); every run pauses after 5 consecutive errors of the test's _NoVerifier, so the test has exactly 5 decisions and fails when none is a successful api action. The hook path raised nothing, costs 0.07 s per run and draws no random numbers; it is now wrapped so it can never fail learn() or a checkpoint. Hook unchanged (docs/change_requests/DX.md). [DX, G2L-6] Credit side of the integration done: CreditAssigner.attach_experiments(registry) makes every ContinualLearner.learn() copy the caller's experiment records into the experience store before the held-out split is refreshed and run evaluate_experiments() after the update: compare_with_experiment on every randomised experiment whose arms have >= 2 matured held-out units (held out by lifetime, paired SE, unchanged), then the selection whenever that held-out measurement changes; when it cannot run, credit_selection.jsonl gets the reason per experiment and arm (assigned units, no final return, lifetime trained on, not randomised). Tested end to end with a test agent keeping its experiments in a real predict.registry.ExperimentRegistry (selection runs on held-out lifetimes; with holdout_experiments=False / one-unit experiments it does not and says why) and, -m slow, with the real CamLiveAgent plus the one line of change request DX-1. NOT done in the agent: DX-1 (agent.py, INT3A) is not applied, so the integrated agent still never evaluates its experiments; with DX-1 applied the selection still does not run there as configured (each agent experiment has one randomised decision; holdout_experiments=False makes every experiment lifetime trained on) and the log says so. Earlier (D fix stage, G-cl M1): Fix stage (G-cl M1): the comparison is held out by lifetime and enforced in code (experiment lifetimes are never trained on; compare_with_experiment excludes any lifetime an estimator or the learner trained on and records it); z-scores use the paired standard error of estimate - measurement on the same units; a zero / undefined standard error is refused. Re-run (diagnostics.json, estimators trained on 288 unregistered lifetimes, validated on 288 held-out experiment lifetimes of 6 experiments): NO estimator is promoted, the default stays 'simple'. RUDDER: RMSE 3.402, mean z^2 6.61, sign agreement 1.0; COCOA: RMSE 4.234, mean z^2 13.84, sign agreement 1.0 (gate mean z^2 <= 3). The earlier 'rudder promoted' was in-sample and is withdrawn. RUDDER's experiment estimate is the decomposer's prediction difference after the first decision, whose latent is the same in every lifetime of every mechanism (identical initial context): it can only estimate an average effect, while the six mechanisms' measured effects differ. The simple attribution has no estimate for a decision without linked outcomes, so it cannot be scored on these experiments. One seed, debug scale. In the synthetic selection test (held-out lifetimes, paired SE) RUDDER passes (mean z^2 about 1.0) and learned COCOA coefficients fail (about 28).

CL-01.limitations: Fix stage (G-cl M2): history is append-only: update() raises ImmutableHistoryError for any change of the decision (candidates, probabilities, time, decision-time diagnostics), context refs, goal, family, provenance, seq, an executed result, a stored final outcome or a query definition (a needs_approval placeholder result may be replaced once; outcomes, queries, annotations, credit, eligibility, labels, intrinsic rewards and windows may change); every read checks ten index columns against the decoded body (StoreIntegrityError, verify_index). The check decodes the stored record on every update: store throughput is lower (store_benchmark in measured.json; measured on a heavily loaded machine). Durability was tested against SIGKILL of the writer, not against power loss (synchronous=FULL is set but cannot be tested here). Unreferenced blobs are never garbage-collected. No retention/deletion policy for authorised data-retention rules (spec 10.4) yet. Success/failure labels are derived heuristically unless set explicitly (set_success).

CL-05.limitations: Fix stage (G-cl m6): metrics count only by provenance (INDEPENDENT_PROVENANCE); internal-reward and unknown provenances are ignored whatever the name; promote_learner declares the provenance of the learner's held-out losses per provider. A plain number is the caller's declaration (validation / retention); only undeclared numbers named like the internal reward are still ignored by name. Promotion and rollback are wired to the learner's held-out validation losses and to measured forgetting and tested on the real model at debug scale; the integrated agent calls promote_learner (agent.py; G2-learn CL-05), and the 'independent validation' is the learner's own held-out split of stored experience, not a separate evaluation service. Experience is never rolled back. [DX, change request INT3A-5, G2L-8] With val_split='record' (the agent's setting) the held-out split is stratified within each objective: its k-th stored record is held out iff floor(u + (k+1) f) > floor(u + k f) (u = seeded hash of the objective, f = val_fraction): exactly every 1/f-th record, so an objective with >= ceil(1/f) = 7 records always has held-out records (before: independent hash per record, a 14-record objective had none with probability 0.85^14 = 0.10); deterministic given the seed and the append-only history, one side per record. promote_learner states the held-out evidence in the decision (PromotionDecision.held_out: evidence, held-out records per provider, providers with a held-out loss; logged) and a refusal for lack of it says 'no held-out evidence: ...' explicitly (fail closed, as the slow-step guard). The objective split (val_split='objective', D's lab) is unchanged. G2-learn's probe_promotion_evidence.py --reps 5: before 3 of 5 first promotions granted (2 refused: the first lifetime had no held-out record), after 5 of 5 granted.

CL-06.limitations: Verified for the learner (model, optimizers, fast state, schedules, sampler, RNG, provider state) at debug scale on the CPU: kill -9 in the middle of an update and in the middle of a checkpoint write, resume in a new process, bit-identical subsequent updates. Bit-identity holds when the experience store holds what it held at the checkpoint (the store is never rolled back; experience written after the checkpoint is kept and would change later batches). CU-20.limitations: Primitive operations can be assigned to procedure steps only when per-step results with time intervals are supplied (PrimitiveOp has no step id: change request D-4). The credit-once guarantee covers outcomes that pass through CreditLedger; estimators that write record.credit directly (simple, rudder) are not forced through it yet. No policy is trained on these records here.

NA-08.limitations: Shown at debug scale (tiny random backbone, debug core) on LabWorld diagnostic experience, and as single updates on Qwen3-4B + the 50m core. No learning curve exists for the real configuration and none on live experience. The prediction loss used in D's evidence is D's local wrapper of Workstream B's stage-1 world heads. Held-out mean NLL 2.981 -> 2.291 (change -0.690 +- 0.259 SE, n=151); the median did not improve (1.902 -> 2.106) and 0.50 of the held-out records improved: the gain is in the over-confident tail. The integrated agent constructs and calls the learner (agent.py; G2-learn NA-08 verified).

CL-02.limitations: The behavioural probe is whatever probes the agent registers (D's evidence: belief / decision latents, D's wrapper of B's world predictions, B's stage-1 policy head). The policy head is not trained by any loss D owns, so its probabilities move only through the latents. Loss shares, strata and the behaviour flag live as JSON in LearningUpdateRecord.notes (change request D-11).

CL-03.limitations: [DX round 2, G2-learn round 2 / G2L-9] The held-out guard measured artefacts: the slow step's own loss evaluation updated running statistics (the world model's KindNormaliser buffers and the target RealScaler) so the held-out loss after the step was in other units, and COCOA's held-out loss used random Poisson bootstrap weights. Fixed: the slow step restores model buffers and providers' heads.scaler after its loss evaluation (it changes the adapters only), COCOA's held-out evaluation is deterministic. G2L-9: minimum tolerance 1e-4 of the provider's held-out loss (micro vetoes were 1e-7..5.4e-5, the smallest real degradation 4.4e-4); per-provider drift bound max(0.02, 2 % of the loss). Also: PCGrad + max_share 0.9 combination of the providers' adapter gradients, the applied AdamW update projected first-order non-increasing for every provider with an adapter gradient and for COCOA (sensitivity gradient on its training records), a verdict-driven trust region (refusal halves the next step to >= 1/16, acceptance grows it by 1.5). Measured with G2-learn's probe_slow_acceptance.py: debug integrated agent (8 lifetimes, two seed sets) kept 14/53 slow steps before, 58/62 after (Fisher p 2e-14); per-step held-out change of the world model median 2e-2 -> 5e-6 relative, COCOA 4e-2 -> 6e-7; D's lab 20/27 -> 27/27; real configuration (Qwen3-4B + 50m core, CUDA, 3 lifetimes) 4/8 kept (G2-learn: 0/6, 1/7), every refusal by the grounding loss's own held-out rise (0.09-0.28 %), the restore found the normaliser and scaler moved in all 8 steps. Net adapter change stays small where promotions are refused for forgetting (rollbacks). Whether adapter updates improve semantic understanding is still NOT shown. Earlier (DX round 1): [DX, G2L-4, G2L-5] The held-out guard fails closed and judges every provider: a slow step is deferred (not taken) while no provider has held-out validation records; a loss without held-out records of its own is removed from the adapter gradient (and the step deferred if no validated loss remains); a held-out loss that cannot be computed after the step rejects it; the step is kept only if, for EACH provider with held-out records, the paired change of its held-out loss over its validation chunks is <= min(0.01, 5 % of its loss, max(2 SE, float floor)) and its summed change since the last promoted checkpoint is <= 0.02; a rejected step is undone with its AdamW state, learning rate, schedule and counters. The verdict lists by_provider, judged and unjudged providers (providers with training data but no held-out records). [DX] Providers are asked eligible(record) without the learner's own flags: before, predict.providers read the learner's held-out exclusion as permanent, so held-out records lost their val: flag at the next refresh (in G2-learn's agent probe only rudder / cocoa / bridge_grounding had held-out losses; now 8 providers). Measured in that probe (3 short lifetimes, tiny configuration): 11 slow steps, 0 without a verdict, 8 reverted (one validation chunk per provider -> float-floor tolerance), 3 kept (clean export of e4186c8: 7 attempted, 2 deferred, 0 without a verdict, 3 of 5 reverted). Whether adapter updates improve semantic understanding is still NOT shown. The adapter graph covers the newest grad_last context items plus all candidate and goal texts (change request D-8).

CL-04.limitations: Regenerated (diagnostics.json): NLL increase on A naive 1.768 +- 0.426, with retention 0.357 +- 0.135; decision agreement on A 0.34 vs 0.86. One pair of LabWorld families at debug scale, one seed. 'Decision agreement' is measured on B's stage-1 policy head, which no loss in this experiment trains. The retention arm combines family-balanced replay with the functional regulariser; their separate contributions were not measured. Anchors are chosen by the caller (first records of a family), not by an importance criterion. Adapters are not covered by the functional regulariser (the slow guard and weight decay protect them).

CL-08.limitations: The learner schedules fast / frequent / slow; the fourth timescale (meta-update of the reward) belongs to Workstream C and is not scheduled here. 'Informative' is decided from the stored surprise of a registered prediction (outcomes nobody predicted always count); the independence unit is the top-level decision, not a statistical test. In D's evidence only the first plan comes from poll(); the remaining updates of each experiment are explicit replay plans.

CL-10.limitations: 15.2 item -> checkpoint content: model weights / semantic adapters / intrinsic reward weights -> weights/<group>.safetensors (every trainable group incl. reward); optimizer state -> optim/<name>.pt (learner groups + extra optimizers, e.g. the agent's reward_meta); fast adaptive state -> fast_state.pt; current task -> state.json current_task; replay indices -> replay_state (sampler stream position, head); experiment records -> state.json experiments [DX]; pending outcomes -> pending_outcomes (the unresolved queries) [DX] + pending_pointer; learning schedules -> schedules (counters, lr schedule steps, guard state); random seeds -> rng.pt (python / numpy / torch CPU+CUDA generators) + config seed; authorization configuration -> auth_config_hash (checked with expected_auth_hash on load) + the task's auth_scope in current_task; model versions -> model_version / reward_version, MANIFEST group hashes and architecture signature. Atomic (temp dir, fsync, rename; crash at every step and kill -9 tested); every tensor is moved to the CPU before writing (GPU test runs only where CUDA is available). Limits: the authorization configuration itself stays with the authorization service (a learner checkpoint cannot restore authorization), and agent.save passes no auth_config_hash (change request DX-2 note); experiments and pending queries live durably in the experience store, the checkpoint copy is for consistency checks / repair (restore writes back experiment records the store lacks, never replaces one it holds, and reports pending queries missing in the store); power-loss durability not tested; integrated restart is INT2's / INT3's evidence, not re-run by DX. [DX round 2] credit.checkpoint.auth_config_hash(task) (sha256 of the task's authorization fields as the learner sees them) and the agent diff (change request DX-2: capture_learner(auth_config_hash=...), restore_learner(expected_auth_hash=...)); with DX-1 the agent's experiment records are copied into the store before every checkpoint. Both are agent.py changes not applied at the time of writing, so CL-10 stays partial for the integrated agent (G2-learn R2.4). Retention: CheckpointManager keeps optimizer state only in the newest kept checkpoint (keep_optim=1, cam_live.storage policy); a rollback to a checkpoint without it starts the learner's optimizers fresh.

The policy head is not trained by any loss in this workstream (the policy loss belongs to Workstream C); credited returns are consumed by the policy update since INT3A's KF-E01 (4476c27; G2-learn G2L-7).
Retention: one family pair, one seed, debug scale; replay and functional regularisation not ablated separately; no anchor-selection criterion.
Estimator comparison: six experiments, one seed, one mechanism family, debug scale.
RUDDER auxiliary losses of the original paper are not implemented; COCOA has no learned outcome encoder and no sampled-alternatives estimator; trajectories longer than 64 decisions are truncated.
No garbage collection of unreferenced blobs and no data-retention / deletion policy in the store.
The learner is single-threaded and assumes it is the only writer of the store.
Estimator selection on LabWorld promotes nothing once validated on held-out lifetimes; RUDDER's per-experiment estimate cannot distinguish mechanisms that share the same first-decision context.
scientific_failures: Return-conditioned hindsight is biased, as the literature says: relative bias 0.061 on the enumerated NoisyKeyDoor and exactly 16/81 on the two-armed bandit with rewards (1, -2). It is kept only as a counterexample.

The redistributed return-to-go gives no variance reduction over REINFORCE at the key decision (key-to-door variance 8.09 for both); the reduction comes only from the contributions of a well-trained decomposer (0.14) or from COCOA (0.059).

Exploratory, not part of the regenerated evidence: in one seeded run of the synthetic experiment world a decomposer trained with a constant learning rate gave arm-difference estimates that disagreed with the randomised differences (RMSE 0.096, mean z^2 4.3); with cosine annealing it agreed. It shows sensitivity to training quality, not a rate.

Learned COCOA coefficients are the less accurate of the two learned estimators on the synthetic experiments (regenerated, held-out lifetimes: max error against the true effect 0.208 versus 0.036 for RUDDER contributions; RMSE against measured differences 0.158 versus 0.044).

Debug-scale credit comparison, held out by lifetime with paired standard errors (regenerated): neither learned estimator passes: RUDDER mean z^2 6.61 (RMSE 3.40), COCOA 13.84 (RMSE 4.23); gate 3.0; default stays 'simple'. The 'rudder promoted' of the earlier recorded run came from in-sample validation (G-cl M1) and is withdrawn.
Held-out prediction (regenerated): mean NLL improved (2.981 -> 2.291) but the median did not (1.902 -> 2.106); 0.50 of held-out records improved.

On the 50m core a single Adam step moves the belief latent a lot: with the 8-step warm-up (first step at lr/8) the probe belief changed by 0.265 mean absolute (real_update.json); without warm-up, at lr 3e-4, by 0.78 (exploratory, measured before the warm-up default; not regenerated).

On Qwen3-4B the world-NLL gradient that reaches LoRA through the semantic embeddings is tiny next to the grounding loss (by-loss adapter gradient norms in real_update.json: bridge_grounding 5.547, world 0.00101): in practice the slow update is driven by the grounding loss.

Update times on the real configuration depend strongly on what else the shared machine is doing: in the regenerated real_update.json (machine under load) the frequent update took 8.6 s and the slow update 9.7 s; the earlier light-load run took 0.73 s and 2.6 s.

Exploratory observation (not regenerated): an untrained ensemble under loss *ascent* first improved the ensemble-mixture NLL on held-out data (members spread apart) before it got worse: per-member NLL (the training objective) and mixture NLL (what is scored) can move in opposite directions for a few updates.

With held-out lifetimes and the paired standard error, learned COCOA coefficients that passed the in-sample synthetic selection test (old measured.json: mean z^2 1.53) fail it (regenerated: 28.3): their bias is several standard errors. RUDDER passes (1.00).

The history check of SqliteExperienceStore.update decodes and compares the stored record: durable add_outcome throughput fell from about 90 to 58 per second in a same-load A/B run of bench_store.py (old vs new replay.py, two runs each); appends and sampling are unchanged.
